answer: Make action rights scarce and collision-forced. Each epoch the economy mints a fixed pool of action permits that identities must hold to transact; permits are finite, like timber. Clones cannot mirror the demand of real agents: a farm's thousand mouths all chase the same permits, bid against each other, and collide — each new clone strictly shrinks the farm's per-identity throughput, like sails catching the same zephyr and stealing each other's wind. Honest agents each catch enough wind; the farm stalls on its own arithmetic.
